description: Conservative first policy for the hybrid physical-header/canonical-payload Step 15 contract. The policy exposes only packet-scoped header fields whose modification does not redefine the selected flow identity, TCP byte ownership, packet length, checksum materialization, or TCP state translation.

rules.rationale: IPv4 TOS/DSCP/ECN is packet scoped and does not define the flow identity, payload ownership, transport byte stream or packet length. It is still bounded because ECN/DSCP semantics exist.
TTL is packet scoped and routinely changes in transit. It must remain non-zero to avoid creating an expired packet.
The advertised TCP receive window is packet scoped and does not change byte ownership, sequence space or flow identity. It remains constrained because extreme values can affect transport behavior.
IPv4 total length and checksum are deterministic consequences of packet materialization and accepted edits.
TCP sequence/acknowledgement numbers, data offset and checksum must be translated or recomputed deterministically after payload/header materialization.
These fields define link/network/transport identity or parser selection. Editing them would change the selected conversation or invalidate downstream traceability.
Fragmentation and TCP control flags affect reassembly, state transitions, stream ownership or urgent data semantics. They are kept immutable in v1.
